summary: Portable equatorial refractor after Saegmuller's 1888 mounting (US 395,002): refracting tube with objective cell, finder, rack-and-pinion focuser, drawtube and eyepiece in a cradle with two tube bands; declination and polar axes, each with a housing, a worm wheel and worm with a slow-motion handle, and a graduated circle; counterweights; latitude pivot on the pier head; turned pier on a three-legged base with leveling screws
views: side elevation, partly in section (Fig. 1): tube, finder, drawtube, eyepiece, both axis housings with their circles and gearing, slow-motion handles, top of the pier
detail section at the eyepiece end of the tube (Fig. 3)

questions: 1. How big should the model be? I would make a desk-size model with a 136 mm main tube, 24 mm across, so that every part prints on its own and the assembly drawing stays at 1:2.5.

2. The sheet cuts off the objective end and the lower pier. I would add an objective cell, a dew shield, a turned pier on a three-legged base with leveling screws, and two counterweights, as on portable equatorials of the period. OK?
3. Polar axis elevation? I would use 40 degrees (about Washington, D.C.), with the tube pointing 35 degrees up.
4. Gears and worms: I would keep 30 square teeth per wheel, plain rings on the worms and 24 rim notches on the circles, with no optics. OK?
5. Printer: I would use the defaults (220 x 220 x 250 mm bed, 0.4 mm nozzle).
assumedAnswers: No user to ask: every answer above is taken as the proposed default and recorded as an assumed dimension and an assumption in model.json.
